                                                                                                 material for a base, army, or corps. This platoon may operate a depot.

                                                                                                 operate forward depots.

                                                                                              Capability: Capable of predicting river stages and discharges, and
                                                                                                 natural and artificial flood velocities, depths, and widths, in a drainage
                                                                                                 basin with an area up to 1,000 square miles; preparing hydrologic
                                                                                                 analyses of river crossings sites; preparing studies of hydrologic and
                                                                                                 hydraulic factors involved in military installations from a point of
                                                                                                 view of flood incidence; providing technical advice on hydraulic
                                                                                                 features of logistic operations and on equipment for use in water.
                                                                                                 When necessary the theater commander will provide for the allocation
                                                                                                 of additional communication facilities and for joint operation of Air
                                                                                                 Weather Service Units and Corps of Engineers units.

                                                                                              Basis of Allocation: Normally one per field army or independent corps;
                                                                                                 may be assigned to a geographic area, determined by stream and
                                                                                                 drainage basin characteristics.

                                                                                              Capability: Provides qualified personnel with equipment for the collec-
                                                                                                 tion, evaluation, and dissemination of terrain data, the production of
                                                                                                military terrain studies, and for consultant services in military geology
                                                                                                and hydrology.

                                                                                              Basis of Allocation : Normally one per field army.

as ravines, valleys, or depressions. All shelters     the weather.

11—9. Classification                                   stades of this type are usually artificial and

Obstacles are divided into two general classes         ious warning devices. They are intended primar-
depending on whether they are existing or are          ily to prevent the enemy from making a surprise
constructed for the express purpose of hindering       assault from areas close to a position.
movement.
                                                             (2) Defensive. Defensive obstacles are ob-
   a. Natural. A natural obstacle is any existing      stacles used to delay the enemy force in areas
object or condition that is used to hinder move-       where it can be engaged with heavy, intense
ment including manmade objects not constructed         defensive fire. They may be either natural or
as obstacles but used as such. Natural obstacles       artificial. A defended roadblock or an obstacle
include swamps, rivers and streams, mountain           in front of a defensive position which stops or
ranges, climatic conditions, irrigation canals, and    delays the enemy force once it is in range of
existing buildings or walls.                           defensive weapons are examples of this type.
                                                       Defensive obstacles should be covered by appro-
  b. Artificial. An artificial obstacle is any man-    priate fire, kept under observation, and should be
made object constructed to hinder movement.            employed in conj unction with protective obstacles.
Artificial obstacles include minefields, antitank
ditches, contaminated areas, hedgehogs, road                 (3) Tactical. Tactical obstacles are ob-
craters, demolished bridges, and barbed wire. It       stacles used to break up enemy attack forma-
may be constructed entirely on land or partially       tions and channelize the enemy force into areas
under water as in the case of beach and river line     where it is blocked by defensive obstacles or can
obstacles.                                             be brought under intensive defensive fires. This
                                                       tactical obstacle delays, harasses, or demoralizes
  c. Uses. Obstacles can be divided into three         the enemy by forcing it to employ dangerous or
groups according to their uses. Seldom does an         exhaustive breaching measures in areas not
obstacle fall clearly into one of these three groups.  covered by fire.
More often than not an obstacle serves in two
or all three capacities. This arbitrary classifica-

       ±                                                                                            In the accompanying diagram, the maximum bending

      Typical crew: Hand work—1 crew leader, 4 to 8 men with brushhooks and axes, 1 to 2 men with portable chain saws.

      Typical crew: 1 crew leader at pit, 1 end loader and 6 dump trucks loading and hauling: crew leader and dumper at site, 1 dozer spreading, 1
tractor and 1 sheepsfoot tandem roller and 1 water wagon spreading and compacting. Number of trucks for each end loader will vary with length
of haul. More than one spread of end loader and trucks may be used to advantage if borrow pit and site are large enough to work additional equip-
ment and work quantity warrants it.

      Typical crew: Scraper work—1 crew leader at pit, 2 or more scrapers with 1 or more pusher tractors. Spreading and compacting crew would
be the same as noted above for work performed with end loader and dump trucks.

      Note. Either method of operation will require a bulldozer part to full time in pit and grader part to full time on haul roads. Embankment
should be smoothed at quitting time and preferably rolled to seal against moisture when there is a possibility of rain. Embankment should be sloped
so that it will drain at all times during construction.

      Scraper operation will normally require less man-hours per cubic yard but is efficient only for short hauls of 4000 feet or less.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Note:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1. Column 3> division of GM and SM groups into subdivisions of d and u are for roada and airfields only. Subdivision is on basis of Atterberg limits; suffix d (e.g., GMd) will be used when
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       the liquid limit is 25 or less and the plasticity Index is 5 or less; the suffix u will be used otherwise.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               2. In the first 7 items of colxmms 7 and 8, where gravel, gravelly solle, sands, or sandy soils are used in an unsurfaced area, they should be stabilized to prevent aircraft dmnage from loose particles. Landing mat will not usually be
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       required on these soils. Where landing mat is used which does not have a flat bottom surface, a cushion layer of fine sand or some other similar fine-grained material will be required for seating of the mat.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               3. In column 12, the equiiment listed will usually produce the required densities with a reasonable number of passes when moisture conditions and thickness of lift are properly controlled. In some
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       instances, several types of equipment are listed because variable soil characteristics within a given soil group may require different equipnent. In some instances, a combination of two types may be necessary.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       a. Unsurfaced areas. Steel-wheeled and rubber-tired rollers are recommended for hard, angular materials with limited fines or screenings. Rubber-tired equipment is reconanended for softer materials.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       b. Areas to be surfaced with landing mat. Rubber-tired equipment is recommended for rolling during final shaping operations for most soils and processed materials.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       £. Equiiment size. The following sizes of equipment are necessary to assure the high densities required for airfield construction:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Crawler-type tractor -• total weight In excess of 30,000 lb.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Rubber-tired equipment -- wheel load in excess of 15,000 lb, wheel loada as high as to,000 lb may be necessary to obtain the required densities for some materials (based on contact pressure of approximately 65 to 150 psi )
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Sheepsfoot roller — unit pressure (on 6- to 12-sq-in. foot) to be in excess of 250 psi and unit pressures as high as 650 pel may be necessary to obtain the required densities for some materials. The area of the feet should
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      be at least 5 percent of the total peripheral area of the drum, using the dimeter measured to the faces of the feet,

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               i». Column 13, unit dry weights are for compacted soil at optimum moisture content for-CE 55 (modified AASHO) compaction effort.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               5* Coliann lit, NA indicates that the airfield index Is greater than 15> This is the maximum value which can be measured by the airfield cone penetrometer.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               6. Columns 9 *nd 10, wet or demp soils are essentially free from dust.

Note:

1. Column 3 division of GM «nri SM groups into subdivisions of d amd u are for roads and airfields only. Subdivision is on basis of Atterberg limits; suffix d (e.g., GMd) will be used when the liquid limit is 25 ot less and the

plasticity index Is 5 cr less; the suffix u will be used otherwise.

2. In column 13, the equipment listed will usually produce the required dmsltles with a reasonable number of passes when moisture conditions and thickness of lift are properly controlled. In some instances, several types of equipment

are listed because variable soil characteristics within a given soil group may require different equipment. In some instances, a combination of two types may be necessary.

a. Processed HAP*» materials And other angular materials. Steel-wheeled and rubber-tired rollers are recommended for hard, angular materials with limited fines or screenings. Rubber-tired equipment is recommended for softer materials

           subject to degradation.

b. Finishing. Rubber-tired equipment is recommended for rolling during final shaping operations for most soils and processed materials.

c. Equipment sime. The following sizes of equipment are necessary to assure the high densities required for airfield construction:

“          Crawler-type tractor -- total weight in excess of 30,000 lb.

           Rubber-tired equipment — wheel load in excess of 15,000 lb. wheel loads as high as 1*0,000 lb may be necessary to obtain the required densities for seme materials (based on contact pressure of approximately 65 to 150 psi).

           Sheepsfoot roller -- unit pressure (on 6- to 12-sq-ln. foot; to be in excess of 250 psi and unit pressures as high as 650 psi may be necessary to obtain the required densities for some materials. The 'area of the feet should

           be at least 5 per cent of the total peripheral area of the drum, using the diameter measured to the faces of the feet.

3. Column lU, unit dry weights are for compacted soil at optimum moisture content for modified AASH0 compaction effort.

1*. In column 15, the maximum value that can be used in design of airfields is, in some cases, limited by gradation and plasticity requirements.
